anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers f5 cleanly: it names the last own push at 12:00 and the non-renewing 12:10 base observation, exits via the 'Deadline elapsed with binding checks' obstacle row, runs no `gh pr checks --watch`, spends no round or sync, and its row 1 `deliver` explicitly opens exactly one more 15-minute window with 'neither cap extended (rounds 0 of 6, syncs 0 of 6)', while no `wait` row appears and stop is recommended last. Before failed the same fact because, despite narrating 'no watch, no renewal' and calling it an obstacle, it still rendered an ordinary `wait` row as row 1 `[recommended]` and offered no numeric deliver continuation, so the 'ordinary wait is absent' and 'later numeric deliver opens one window' clauses did not hold. Nothing in After regressed a fact Before kept; to keep it that way, retain the explicit per-row cap/round accounting text on the deliver row and the 'Not offered: merge' line, since those are what let a reader verify the one-window/no-extension claim without inferring it from the narration.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before fails f5 because it renders an ordinary `wait - start a new bounded CI watch` row as the recommended option, so the expired deadline leads back to a watch rather than an obstacle menu, and no numeric deliver with a single bounded extension exists. After moves f5 to holds: it computes the deadline as expired after the 12:00 own push, runs no `gh pr checks --watch` and does not renew on the 12:10 base observation, exits `stuck - CI pending past 15 minutes`, and renders deliver (exactly one additional 15-minute window), assess, and stop-recommended-last with an explicit `Neither cap is extended` line and no wait row. One nit to tighten: the rendered `Verdict: fixable - CI pending past 15 minutes` sits awkwardly beside the `stuck -` exit; naming the verdict as an obstacle (e.g. `Verdict: obstacle - CI pending past 15 minutes`) would make the obstacle rendering unambiguous to a reader without changing any other behavior.
